Modified assessment incorporating literature:
- Policy stance and interest-rate smoothing: By holding the funds rate at 1–1.25% yet reiterating “gradual increases” and that the policy rate will remain “below…longer run” for some time, the Committee is acting in line with inertial Taylor-rule behavior and interest-rate smoothing emphasized in Clarida, Galí, and Gertler (estimated policy rules) and the broader New Keynesian literature. This combination signals a mild tightening bias without abrupt moves.
- Inflation framework: With 12-month inflation below 2% and a “symmetric” target, the stance is consistent with flexible inflation forecast targeting (Svensson and Woodford). Looking through hurricane-related, transitory price spikes aligns with the literature on supply shocks and the cost channel (Christiano, Eichenbaum, and Evans; Ravenna and Walsh), which cautions against overreacting to temporary, energy-driven inflation.
- Balance sheet normalization: Announcing runoff initiation in October is a modestly hawkish step toward policy normalization. Given evidence that QE affects term premia but has limited impact on real growth on its own, tapering reinvestments likely tightens financial conditions slightly while relying on forward guidance to anchor expectations.
- Implementation mechanics: The IOER/ON RRP settings to keep the funds rate in range reflect modern floor/corridor system design (Goodfriend), reinforcing controlled, predictable implementation consistent with forward-guidance frameworks that influence the entire yield curve.

Net tone: Slightly more hawkish than a pure hold due to the start of balance sheet normalization and maintained guidance for gradual hikes, tempered by below-target inflation and explicit symmetry around 2%.
